newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah wins four seats in south Lebanon vote.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah wins four seats in south Lebanon vote.

text.p: A joint ticket headed by Lebanon's two most powerful Shi'ite Moslem groups swept to victory in the fourth round of the country's parliamentary elections, according to partial and unofficial results on Monday.
The list formed by the secular movement Amal and the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) swept all 23 seats contested in Sunday's vote, officials said.

The result gave Hizbollah four deputies in the 128-member parliament while Amal won five seats and a close ally won a sixth. The Amal candidates were headed by Nabih Berri, its chief during its days as a militia in the 1975-90 civil war, who is now speaker of parliament.
The other 13 winners included Bahia Hariri, sister of Sunni Moslem billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, four government ministers and other government supporters.
Two rival lists of leftists and independent traditional politicians failed to gain a seat in parliament.
Amal and Hizbollah, which are rivals in the predominantly Shi'ite south and fought a sporadic war in the late 1980s, formed the joint list on the eve of the polls in a compromise mediated by Syria.

Damascus, whose 35,000 troops in Lebanon give it a powerful say in the country's affairs, was anxious to avoid a straight fight between the two groups which could have erupted in bloodshed, political analysts said.

Hizbollah, whose guerrillas are fighting Israeli troops occupying a south Lebanon border strip, is an important element in Syria's Middle East peace strategy designed to bring an end to Israeli occupation of the Golan Heights and south Lebanon, analysts say.

The fundamentalist group lost two parliamentary seats to government supporters in earlier rounds of the election, giving rise to speculation that Syria had decided that the time had come to weaken it politically.

But the last-minute deal Syria brokered for the south Lebanon election and next Sunday's final round of voting in the eastern Bekaa Valley will give Hizbollah a total of seven deputies and two allies in the new parliament.
This compares with eight deputies and four allies in the outgoing parliament.
